To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we show the existence, uniqueness and differentiability of strong solutions to multi-dimensional mean-field SDEs, with irregular drift coefficients that include the cumulative distribution function.

we show existence, uniqueness and differentiability of solutions to mean-field stochastic differential equation where the drift depends in form of an expectation functional on the law of the process and we give a probabilist representation of the strong derivatives of such solutions with respect to their initial condition.

we prove strong solutions to multi-dimensional mean-field SDEs where the drift depends in an irregular way on the solution's law, we show that these solutions are Malliavin differentable, and we give a representation of their derivative with respect to initial conditions.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the analysis of mean-field stochastic differential equation with irregular expectation functionals in the drift.
a new class of mean-field stochastic differential equation, which includes the classical McKean-Vlasov SDEs as a special case, and provides a new framework for the analysis of such equations.
the study of the regularity properties of strong solutions to mean-field SDEs and their dependence on the initial condition.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the Bismuth-Elworthy-Lie formula for the derivative of expectation functionals with respect to the starting point of a stochastic differential equation holds for a large class of mean-field stochastic differential equation with irregular drift.

we show the existence and uniqueness of strong solutions of mean-field equations with irregular expectation functional and we provide a probabilistic representation for the strong derivative of the solution with respect to its initial value.
we can treat irregular drifts in the sense of Malliavin derivatives, but regular drifts in the initial derivative sense.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we extend the results of the paper by Bismut (1973), Bismut (1984), Elworthy et al. (1990) to the mean-field setting.

we are able to handle drift coefficients which are not necessarily regular in the law of the solution, but are only required to be regular in the cumulative distribution function, or even the probability density function of the solution.

we provide a rigorous framework to deal with mean-field SDEs with drift depending on the cumulative distribution functions of the solutions and show how to compute the derivatives of the solution process and its distribution with respect to its initial condition.
The main takeaway from our work is that

we are able to treat the drift coefficient as an arbitrary function of the law, which in particular allows us to consider the case of the drift depending on the cumulative distribution of the solution.
we can treat mean-field equations with drift depending on the cumulative distribution of the solution in the same way we do for drifts depending on the density of the solution.
the drift can depend on the solution in a very singular way, while still ensuring that the solution is differentiable with respect to its initial condition.
